statements.status_notes: A flaw was found in libssh. If data packets are processed after a channel is closed, channel data callbacks can be invoked after the associated data has already been freed, leading to crashes or possible use-after-free conditions.
statements.impact_statement: libssh-4 is present only as a dependency of libcurl, which links it for scp and sftp URL support. The image ships no ssh, scp or sftp client, nothing in the runtime path invokes curl, and the JRE does not link libssh, so no libssh channel is ever opened by Liquibase Secure. The use-after-free needs data packets arriving on a closed libssh channel, so it is not reachable from Liquibase Secure. Fixed in Ubuntu libssh-4 0.9.6-2ubuntu0.22.04.8 (jammy, shipped by Liquibase Secure 5.0.0 and 5.0.1) and 0.10.6-2ubuntu0.5 (noble, Liquibase Secure 5.0.2 through 5.2.1); Liquibase Secure 5.2.2 and later ship 0.10.6-2ubuntu0.5.

statements.status_notes: jackson-databind contains the general-purpose data-binding functionality and tree-model for Jackson Data Processor. From 2.18.0 until 2.18.9, 2.21.5, 2.22.1, 3.1.5, and 3.2.1, UnwrappedPropertyHandler.processUnwrapped() replays buffered JSON for a @JsonUnwrapped property and calls prop.deserializeAndSet() without a prop.visibleInView(ctxt.getActiveView()) guard, allowing a property annotated with both @JsonView and @JsonUnwrapped to be written from attacker JSON under a less-privileged active view. This issue is fixed in versions 2.18.9, 2.21.5, 2.22.1, 3.1.5, and 3.2.1.
statements.impact_statement: Fixed in jackson-databind 2.18.9, 2.21.5 and 2.22.1. Every published Liquibase Secure image from 5.0.0 through 6.0.0 carries at least one copy inside the advisory range, so this assessment does not rest on version. The copies were read from the PackageVersion class in each shipped jar, including copies relocated inside vendor drivers. In 5.0.x the only affected copy is the one relocated inside snowflake-jdbc (2.18.1). In 5.1.x and 5.2.0 the snowflake-jdbc, databricks-jdbc and Azure SDK copies are on 2.18.x, and 5.2.0 adds the first-party 2.21.2. In 5.2.1 the first-party copies are on 2.22.0 and the Couchbase SDK copy is on 2.21.4. In 5.2.2 and 6.0.0 the first-party copies are fixed and the one affected copy left is 2.18.8, relocated inside databricks-jdbc. The vulnerable path needs a property annotated with both @JsonView and @JsonUnwrapped, deserialized from attacker JSON under an active view. A scan of every class in every shipped jar, first-party and vendor, found no @JsonView annotation and no view-scoped reader anywhere. The only @JsonUnwrapped use is in a log4j JSON layout, which serializes and never deserializes. Without the annotation pair, the unchecked view gate is never reached.

statements.status_notes: sqlparse is a non-validating SQL parser module for Python. Prior to 0.6.0, SQL_REGEX in sqlparse/keywords.py and the per-position loop in sqlparse/lexer.py repeatedly scan unmatched dollar-quoted literal and multiline-comment delimiters, causing quadratic CPU consumption through sqlparse.parse(), sqlparse.format(), and sqlparse.split(). This issue is fixed in version 0.6.0.
statements.impact_statement: sqlparse is pinned at 0.5.3 in tools/liquibase-checks/liquibase-checks/pom.xml:864. The surrounding build plugin comment states these Python packages are only needed at build time and are never used at runtime (tools/liquibase-checks/liquibase-checks/pom.xml:893, tools/liquibase-checks/liquibase-checks/pom.xml:895), and the runtime implementation only references sqlparse in explanatory comments about a possible Python lock hang (tools/liquibase-checks/liquibase-checks/src/main/java/com/liquibase/executor/PythonScriptExecutor.java:77, tools/liquibase-checks/liquibase-checks/src/main/java/com/liquibase/executor/PythonScriptExecutor.java:240). The only actual import is in a test fixture (tools/liquibase-checks/liquibase-checks/src/test/resources/scripts/badScript.py:4). NVD and GitHub both describe this as a sqlparse DoS fixed in 0.6.0, but the vulnerable parser is not reachable from the Liquibase runtime.

statements.status_notes: sqlparse is a non-validating SQL parser module for Python. Prior to 0.6.0, sqlparse/filters/output.py fails to escape existing backslashes before quotes in sqlparse.format output_format='python' and output_format='php' and the corresponding sqlformat -l modes, allowing crafted SQL to terminate the generated string and inject Python or PHP code when a downstream consumer executes or imports the generated source. This issue is fixed in version 0.6.0.
statements.impact_statement: sqlparse ships in the runtime virtual environment of the checks module's embedded Python scripting engine, which end users can use to author custom check scripts; the build only strips pip, setuptools, and their installer machinery from that environment, not sqlparse itself. None of the check scripts Liquibase bundles and runs by default import sqlparse — they use a different SQL parsing library for changeset SQL. The vulnerable Python/PHP output-formatting code path (sqlparse.format with output_format='python' or 'php') is only reachable if a customer authors and configures their own custom check script that imports sqlparse and calls it in one of those modes; no shipped configuration does this out of the box.

statements.status_notes: Netty is an asynchronous, event-driven network application framework. Prior to versions 4.1.136.Final and 4.2.16.Final, the newHandshakeResponse methods of WebSocketServerHandshaker07 and WebSocketServerHandshaker08 complete a WebSocket protocol upgrade based solely on the presence of a Sec-WebSocket-Version: 7 (or 8) header, without verifying the mandatory Connection: Upgrade and Upgrade: websocket headers, enabling HTTP request smuggling / protocol-confusion attacks through intermediaries that don't recognize the request as an Upgrade. Fixed in versions 4.1.136.Final and 4.2.16.Final.
statements.impact_statement: WebSocketServerHandshaker07/08 are server-side handshake classes, and neither module ever runs a WebSocket server: liquibase-commercial-cassandra's AWS SDK secretsmanager -> netty-nio-client chain and liquibase-azure's azure-core-http-netty each only make plain HTTPS client calls, never WebSocket connections. Cassandra's copy of netty-codec-http also already resolves at 4.1.137.Final, past the 4.1.136.Final fix line, as secondary defense-in-depth.

statements.status_notes: Netty is an asynchronous, event-driven network application framework. Prior to versions 4.1.136.Final and 4.2.16.Final, HttpContentEncoder maintains a per-channel acceptEncodingQueue that accumulates attacker-controlled data without a size limit; the queue is filled on the I/O thread for every inbound HTTP request and drained only when the application writes a non-1xx response, allowing an attacker to exploit HTTP/1.1 pipelining to exhaust resources. Fixed in versions 4.1.136.Final and 4.2.16.Final.
statements.impact_statement: HttpContentEncoder encodes outbound responses on the server side of an HTTP exchange, a role neither module ever plays: liquibase-commercial-cassandra's AWS SDK secretsmanager -> netty-nio-client chain and liquibase-azure's azure-core-http-netty each only make outbound client requests and decode inbound responses, never run an HTTP server. Cassandra's copy of netty-codec-http also already resolves at 4.1.137.Final, past the 4.1.136.Final fix line, as secondary defense-in-depth.

statements.status_notes: Netty is an asynchronous, event-driven network application framework. Prior to versions 4.1.136.Final and 4.2.16.Final, Netty's HTTP/2-to-HTTP/1.x translation layer (Http2StreamFrameToHttpObjectCodec / InboundHttp2ToHttpAdapter) fails to deduplicate or validate Host headers when an HTTP/2 client supplies both the :authority pseudo-header and a literal host header in a single HEADERS frame, producing an HttpRequest with two differing Host headers that can be used to bypass request-routing logic. Fixed in versions 4.1.136.Final and 4.2.16.Final.
statements.impact_statement: This CVE concerns the HTTP/2-to-HTTP/1.x translation layer a front-end server or proxy uses (e.g. InboundHttp2ToHttpAdapter) to receive and translate inbound HTTP/2 requests — a server/proxy-side concept neither module ever exercises, both being pure outbound HTTP/2 clients: liquibase-commercial-cassandra's AWS SDK secretsmanager -> netty-nio-client chain and liquibase-azure's azure-core-http-netty each only ever act as a direct HTTP/1.1 or HTTP/2 client, never a protocol-translating front end. Cassandra's copy of netty-codec-http2 also already resolves at 4.1.137.Final, past the 4.1.136.Final fix line, as secondary defense-in-depth.

statements.status_notes: Netty is an asynchronous, event-driven network application framework. In versions 4.2.0.Final through 4.2.15.Final and 4.1.0.Final through 4.1.135.Final, Bzip2Decoder's run-length encoding (RLE) state machine can enter an infinite loop when processing a malformed bzip2 stream, permanently occupying the event-loop thread at 100% CPU and causing denial of service. Fixed in versions 4.1.136.Final and 4.2.16.Final.
statements.impact_statement: See CVE-2026-59901 entry on netty-codec above — same root cause (Bzip2Decoder RLE infinite loop), mirrored here so scanners that flag netty-codec-compression (the module Bzip2Decoder lives in for Netty 4.2.x) receive the same not_affected statement. Liquibase dependency management includes Netty versions below the fixed 4.2.16.Final release (cloud-integrations/liquibase-azure-extension/pom.xml:65, cloud-integrations/liquibase-azure-deps/pom.xml:50, commercial-databases/liquibase-commercial-bigquery/pom.xml:72). No Liquibase Netty consumer adds Bzip2Decoder/Bzip2Encoder to a pipeline.

statements.status_notes: Netty is an asynchronous, event-driven network application framework. In versions 4.2.0.Final through 4.2.15.Final and 4.1.0.Final through 4.1.135.Final, Bzip2Decoder's run-length encoding (RLE) state machine can enter an infinite loop when processing a malformed bzip2 stream, permanently occupying the event-loop thread at 100% CPU and causing denial of service. Fixed in versions 4.1.136.Final and 4.2.16.Final.
statements.impact_statement: netty-codec resolves below the 4.1.136.Final fix line for both modules assessed here (4.1.130.Final for liquibase-commercial-cassandra via cassandra-jdbc-wrapper -> java-driver-core, 4.1.135.Final for liquibase-azure via azure-core-http-netty). The vulnerable class, Bzip2Decoder, is never reachable in either: the Cassandra native protocol's compression negotiation supports only LZ4/Snappy and this extension doesn't configure compression at all, while Azure's Netty HTTP client never wires a Bzip2Decoder into any pipeline (Azure HTTP responses use gzip/deflate/br, and a class-listing search of the Azure SDK jars for Bzip-related symbols returns zero hits).

statements.status_notes: Netty is an asynchronous, event-driven network application framework. Prior to 4.1.137.Final and 4.2.17.Final, io.netty.handler.codec.http.cors.CorsHandler's setVaryHeader method replaces application-defined Vary headers (such as Authorization or Cookie) with Origin. This allows a caching proxy or CDN sitting in front of a server using CorsHandler to reuse one user's authenticated response for another user, disclosing sensitive information. Fixed in versions 4.1.137.Final and 4.2.17.Final.
statements.impact_statement: CorsHandler applies CORS response headers on the server side of an HTTP exchange; this repository never runs an HTTP server that uses it. A source review found no references to CorsHandler or CorsConfig anywhere in this repository's own code; every module that bundles netty-codec-http does so only as a transitive dependency of an outbound HTTP client (the AWS SDK's netty-nio-client, the Azure SDK's azure-core-http-netty, the Couchbase Java client, and the Cassandra driver's own AWS SDK chain), never as a server. The AWS extension and the Cassandra extension already resolve netty-codec-http at 4.1.137.Final, past the fix line, as defense-in-depth; the Azure extension remains on the vulnerable 4.1.135.Final and the Couchbase client's shaded copy remains on 4.2.16.Final, both relying solely on the reachability argument.

statements.status_notes: Netty is an asynchronous, event-driven network application framework. Prior to versions 4.1.136.Final and 4.2.16.Final, HttpPostRequestEncoder constructs multipart HTTP request bodies by directly concatenating user-supplied filenames and field names into Content-Disposition MIME headers without validating or sanitizing CRLF characters. Since MIME headers are delimited by CRLF, an attacker who controls the filename can inject arbitrary MIME headers into the multipart body part. Fixed in versions 4.1.136.Final and 4.2.16.Final.
statements.impact_statement: Fixed in netty-codec-http 4.1.136.Final per NVD and GHSA. This repository's current build already resolves netty-codec-http 4.1.136.Final via the Azure extension's Netty HTTP client, past the fix line. This CVE is specific to Netty's HttpPostRequestEncoder multipart body construction from attacker-controlled filenames and field names, but this repository's only multipart upload implementation (S3 object uploads in the AWS extension) uses the AWS SDK's REST-level multipart API (separate part-numbered PUT requests), not Netty's multipart/form-data encoder — a fundamentally different mechanism. A source review found no references to HttpPostRequestEncoder, DiskFileUpload, MemoryFileUpload, or MixedFileUpload anywhere in this repository, so the vulnerable encoder path is not reachable regardless of version.

statements.status_notes: Vulnerability in the Oracle Java SE, Oracle GraalVM for JDK, Oracle GraalVM Enterprise Edition product of Oracle Java SE (component: Security). Supported versions that are affected are Oracle Java SE: 8u491, 8u491-perf, 11.0.31, 17.0.19, 21.0.11, 25.0.3, 26.0.1; Oracle GraalVM for JDK: 17.0.19 and 21.0.11; Oracle GraalVM Enterprise Edition: 21.3.18. Easily exploitable vulnerability allows unauthenticated attacker with network access via multiple protocols to compromise Oracle Java SE, Oracle GraalVM for JDK, Oracle GraalVM Enterprise Edition. Successful attacks of this vulnerability can result in unauthorized update, insert or delete access to some of Oracle Java SE, Oracle GraalVM for JDK, Oracle GraalVM Enterprise Edition accessible data as well as unauthorized read access to a subset of Oracle Java SE, Oracle GraalVM for JDK, Oracle GraalVM Enterprise Edition accessible data. Note: This vulnerability can be exploited by using APIs in the specified Component, e.g., through a web service which supplies data to the APIs. This vulnerability also applies to Java deployments, typically in clients running sandboxed Java Web Start applications or sandboxed Java applets, that load and run untrusted code (e.g., code that comes from the internet) and rely on the Java sandbox for security.
statements.impact_statement: Oracle Java SE Security (java.security) issue, fixed in OpenJDK 21.0.12. The JRE was read from the release file of each published Liquibase Secure image: 5.0.0 and 5.0.1 ship Temurin 21.0.8, 5.0.2 and 5.0.3 ship 21.0.9, 5.1.0 and 5.1.1 ship 21.0.10, 5.2.0 and 5.2.1 ship 21.0.11, 5.2.2 ships 21.0.12+8 and 6.0.0 ships 21.0.12.1+1, so 5.2.2 and later already carry the fix. For the earlier images, exploitation needs an attacker to deliver crafted data to the java.security APIs, either through a network service that passes untrusted input to them or through a sandboxed Java Web Start or applet client that runs untrusted code. Liquibase Secure is neither. It runs as a command-line client that starts no listener, runs no untrusted code, and only connects outbound to the database and service endpoints its operator configures.

statements.status_notes: Vulnerability in the Oracle Java SE, Oracle GraalVM for JDK, Oracle GraalVM Enterprise Edition product of Oracle Java SE (component: Security). Supported versions that are affected are Oracle Java SE: 8u501, 11.0.32, 17.0.20, 21.0.12, 25.0.4, 26.0.2; Oracle GraalVM for JDK: 17.0.20 and 21.0.12; Oracle GraalVM Enterprise Edition: 21.3.19. Difficult to exploit vulnerability allows unauthenticated attacker with network access via multiple protocols to compromise Oracle Java SE, Oracle GraalVM for JDK, Oracle GraalVM Enterprise Edition. Successful attacks of this vulnerability can result in unauthorized read access to a subset of Oracle Java SE, Oracle GraalVM for JDK, Oracle GraalVM Enterprise Edition accessible data. Note: This vulnerability can only be exploited by supplying data to APIs in the specified Component without using Untrusted Java Web Start applications or Untrusted Java applets, such as through a web service. CVSS 3.1 Base Score 3.7 (Confidentiality impacts). CVSS Vector: (CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:H/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:L/I:N/A:N).
statements.impact_statement: JDK Security component (resource resolving) vulnerability, part of Oracle's August 2026 CPU. Liquibase Secure is built from eclipse- temurin:21-jre-noble (docker/Dockerfile:2) and never listens on a socket; it is only an outbound network client (HTTPS to license/hub endpoints, TLS JDBC to target databases). Triggering this requires a compromised or MITM'd peer that Liquibase already trusts and connects to -- not exploitable by an arbitrary remote attacker with no foothold on those endpoints. Fixed upstream in Temurin 21.0.12.1+1, but no eclipse- temurin Docker Hub image publishes that build yet as of 2026-09-22 (all noble/jre/jdk tags remain 21.0.12_8); revisit once Temurin ships an updated 21-jre-noble tag.

statements.status_notes: Vulnerability in the Oracle Java SE, Oracle GraalVM for JDK, Oracle GraalVM Enterprise Edition product of Oracle Java SE (component: Networking). Supported versions that are affected are Oracle Java SE: 8u501, 11.0.32, 17.0.20, 21.0.12, 25.0.4, 26.0.2; Oracle GraalVM for JDK: 17.0.20 and 21.0.12; Oracle GraalVM Enterprise Edition: 21.3.19. Difficult to exploit vulnerability allows unauthenticated attacker with network access via HTTP to compromise Oracle Java SE, Oracle GraalVM for JDK, Oracle GraalVM Enterprise Edition. While the vulnerability is in Oracle Java SE, Oracle GraalVM for JDK, Oracle GraalVM Enterprise Edition, attacks may significantly impact additional products (scope change). Successful attacks of this vulnerability can result in unauthorized access to critical data or complete access to all Oracle Java SE, Oracle GraalVM for JDK, Oracle GraalVM Enterprise Edition accessible data. Note: This vulnerability can be exploited by using APIs in the specified Component, e.g., through a web service which supplies data to the APIs. This vulnerability also applies to Java deployments, typically in clients running sandboxed Java Web Start applications or sandboxed Java applets, that load and run untrusted code (e.g., code that comes from the internet) and rely on the Java sandbox for security. CVSS 3.1 Base Score 6.8 (Confidentiality impacts). CVSS Vector: (CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:H/PR:N/UI:N/S:C/C:H/I:N/A:N).
statements.impact_statement: JDK Networking (HTTP Connections) vulnerability, part of Oracle's August 2026 CPU. Liquibase Secure is built from eclipse-temurin:21-jre-noble (docker/Dockerfile:2) and never listens on a socket; it is only an outbound network client (HTTPS to license/hub endpoints, TLS JDBC to target databases). Triggering this requires a compromised or MITM'd peer that Liquibase already trusts and connects to -- not exploitable by an arbitrary remote attacker with no foothold on those endpoints. Fixed upstream in Temurin 21.0.12.1+1, but no eclipse-temurin Docker Hub image publishes that build yet as of 2026-09-22 (all noble/jre/jdk tags remain 21.0.12_8); revisit once Temurin ships an updated 21-jre-noble tag.

statements.status_notes: MariaDB Connector/J does not enforce allowLocalInfile=false when a server answers a query with a LOCAL INFILE request. When a client runs LOAD DATA LOCAL INFILE, a rogue or man-in-the-middle server can echo the same filename back and the connector sends the file content even though local infile was disabled. The server cannot redirect the request to a different file than the one named in the client's query.
statements.impact_statement: Fixed in mariadb-java-client 3.5.9. Liquibase Secure 5.2.2 and later ship 3.5.9 or newer, which includes the fix. Releases 5.0.0 through 5.2.1 shipped 3.5.6 or 3.5.7 and are affected. Liquibase never sets allowLocalInfile and never issues LOAD DATA LOCAL INFILE itself (the loadData change type sends INSERT statements), so exposure on those releases requires a user who sets allowLocalInfile=false in the JDBC URL, runs LOAD DATA LOCAL INFILE in changelog SQL, and connects to a rogue or man-in-the-middle server. With the driver default (allowLocalInfile=true) the fixed and unfixed drivers behave the same.

statements.status_notes: The deprecated functions ns_printrrf, ns_printrr and fp_nquery in the GNU C Library version 2.0.1 to version 2.43 fail to validate the RDATA content against the RDATA length in a DNS response when processing A6, CERT, LOC, TKEY or TSIG records, which may allow an attacker to craft a DNS response, causing a target application to crash or read uninitialized memory.
statements.impact_statement: The scanned image reports libc-bin 2.35-0ubuntu3.10, below Ubuntu's fixed 2.35-0ubuntu3.14, but this issue affects deprecated glibc debugging helpers for printing DNS record data rather than the resolver path itself. Liquibase Secure's stock runtime is the Liquibase Java CLI, and a source review found no references to ns_printrrf, ns_printrr, fp_nquery, or TSIG-related record-printing in the product runtime path.

statements.status_notes: curl might erroneously pass on credentials for a first proxy to a second proxy.
statements.impact_statement: The scanned image reports curl 7.81.0-1ubuntu1.20, below Ubuntu's fixed 7.81.0-1ubuntu1.24, but this issue requires a libcurl-based application to follow a cross-scheme redirect while using distinct proxies per scheme and proxy credentials on the first proxy. Liquibase Secure's stock container uses wget for its own downloads and executes the Liquibase Java CLI at runtime, and a focused review found no proxy-authenticated libcurl flow, redirect-following, or curl option handling in the product runtime path.

statements.status_notes: Vulnerability in the Oracle Java SE, Oracle GraalVM for JDK, Oracle GraalVM Enterprise Edition product of Oracle Java SE (component: Install). Supported versions that are affected are Oracle Java SE: 8u501, 11.0.32, 17.0.20, 21.0.12, 25.0.4, 26.0.2; Oracle GraalVM for JDK: 17.0.20 and 21.0.12; Oracle GraalVM Enterprise Edition: 21.3.19. Easily exploitable vulnerability allows low privileged attacker with logon to the infrastructure where Oracle Java SE, Oracle GraalVM for JDK, Oracle GraalVM Enterprise Edition executes to compromise Oracle Java SE, Oracle GraalVM for JDK, Oracle GraalVM Enterprise Edition. Successful attacks of this vulnerability can result in takeover of Oracle Java SE, Oracle GraalVM for JDK, Oracle GraalVM Enterprise Edition.
statements.impact_statement: Oracle Java SE/GraalVM Install-component vulnerability, fixed upstream in 21.0.12 (Oracle August 2026 CPU). The flaw is in Oracle's Java installer, a packaging component that ships only with Oracle's own distribution. Liquibase Secure is built from eclipse-temurin:21-jre-noble (core/docker/Dockerfile:1) via docker-entrypoint.sh (core/docker/docker-entrypoint.sh:8); Temurin's JRE is unpacked from a release archive, not installed through Oracle's installer, so the vulnerable component is not present in the image at all. There is no Adoptium/Temurin tracking entry for this CVE. Unlike the other Oracle Java SE entries in this batch (sandbox/Web Start applicability mismatches, justified requires_environment), this is a component absence -- the installer isn't shipped at all -- hence code_not_present.

statements.status_notes: Using libcurl, when a custom Host: header is first set for an HTTP request and a second request is subsequently done using the same easy handle but without the custom Host: header set, the second request would use stale information and pass on cookies meant for the first host in the second request.
statements.impact_statement: The scanned image reports curl 7.81.0-1ubuntu1.20, below Ubuntu's fixed 7.81.0-1ubuntu1.24, but this issue requires a libcurl-based application to reuse the same easy handle across multiple HTTP requests while first setting a custom Host header and later omitting it. Liquibase Secure's stock container uses wget for its own downloads and executes the Liquibase Java CLI at runtime, and a focused review found no custom Host header handling, cookie replay path, or libcurl easy-handle reuse in the product runtime path.

statements.status_notes: OpenSSL CMS decryption sizes the key-unwrap output buffer based on querying the unwrapped key size, but the AES-WRAP-PAD unwrap primitive can write and cleanse more bytes than that query reports, causing an 8-byte out-of-bounds heap write.
statements.impact_statement: The scanned image reports libssl3 3.0.2-0ubuntu1.19, below Ubuntu's fixed 3.0.2-0ubuntu1.29, but this issue is only reachable when an application decrypts attacker-supplied CMS messages through OpenSSL's CMS_decrypt path. Liquibase Secure's stock container runs the Liquibase Java CLI rather than OpenSSL CMS tooling, and a source review found no references to CMS_decrypt, AES-WRAP-PAD CMS unwrapping, or related OpenSSL CMS handling in the product runtime path.

statements.status_notes: The OpenSSL Certificate Management Protocol (CMP) caches additional certificates (extraCerts) sent in a CMP message, but never expunges them if the message is rejected. If a server reuses a single OSSL_CMP_CTX for the lifetime of a server process, a malicious client may flood it with requests and cause unbounded memory growth.
statements.impact_statement: The scanned image reports libssl3 3.0.2-0ubuntu1.19, below Ubuntu's fixed 3.0.2-0ubuntu1.29, but this issue is only reachable when a long- lived CMP server reuses an OSSL_CMP_CTX across attacker-supplied requests and caches extraCerts from rejected messages. Liquibase Secure's stock container runs the Liquibase Java CLI rather than an OpenSSL CMP server, and a source review found no references to OSSL_CMP_CTX, extraCerts, or CMP request processing in the product runtime path.

statements.status_notes: When verifying the password-based MAC protection of a CMP message, OpenSSL reads the protectionAlg algorithm parameter with X509_ALGOR_get0() and treats the returned value as a PBMParameter after checking only that the pointer is not null, without validating the ASN.1 type. A remote attacker can crash an application acting as a CMP server that accepts PBM-protected messages, or a CMP client talking to a malicious or intercepted CMP server, causing a denial of service.
statements.impact_statement: The scanned image reports libssl3 3.0.2-0ubuntu1.19, below Ubuntu's fixed 3.0.2-0ubuntu1.29, but this issue is only reachable when an application verifies CMP password-based protection on attacker-supplied messages. Liquibase Secure's stock container runs the Liquibase Java CLI rather than OpenSSL CMP tooling, and a source review found no references to CMP, PBM, or OSSL_CMP request-processing paths in the product runtime.

statements.status_notes: Calling wordexp with WRDE_APPEND in the GNU C Library version 2.0 to version 2.43 can cause the interface to return invalid memory in the we_wordv member, which on subsequent calls to wordfree may abort the process.
statements.impact_statement: This flaw requires an application to call glibc's wordexp function with the WRDE_APPEND flag. Neither the JVM nor the container's bash entrypoint calls wordexp; this is a C-language shell-word-expansion API that Liquibase Secure's Java and bash-only runtime path never invokes.

statements.status_notes: When asked to both use a .netrc file for credentials and follow HTTP redirects, libcurl could leak the password used for the first host to the followed-to host under certain circumstances.
statements.impact_statement: The scanned image reports curl 7.81.0-1ubuntu1.20, below Ubuntu's fixed 7.81.0-1ubuntu1.24, but this issue requires a libcurl-based application to combine .netrc credential loading with HTTP redirect following. Liquibase Secure's stock container uses wget for its own downloads and executes the Liquibase Java CLI at runtime, and a focused review found no libcurl, .netrc, or redirect-handling path in the container build or runtime entrypoint.

statements.status_notes: Apache HttpComponents Client, when using the classic (blocking) I/O model, fails to release the underlying connection back to the connection manager if the response contains an invalid or unsupported Content-Encoding header value. Repeated requests to a malicious or misbehaving server leak connections and eventually exhaust the connection pool, producing a denial of service. The async I/O model is not affected. Fixed in version 5.6.3.
statements.impact_statement: httpclient5 is already pinned to 5.6.4 (past the 5.6.3 fix), but that alone only holds until a future downgrade, so we also checked reachability of the classic (blocking) client this CVE affects. Two usages exist: a bundled PII-detection filter, which is unreachable - it requires a policy-loading path Liquibase's checks engine never invokes - and the AWS SDK's synchronous Secrets Manager client, which is real but only ever talks to AWS's own TLS-authenticated endpoint. Exploitation needs that server to repeatedly send malformed Content-Encoding responses, so a remote attacker can't trigger this without already controlling or intercepting trusted AWS traffic - the same precondition used for the related Netty HTTP/2 CVEs.

statements.status_notes: Improper Access Control, Incorrect Authorization vulnerability in Apache Tomcat leads to security constraint bypass if a constraint for a longer path is specified before a more restrictive constraint for a shorter sub-path. This issue affects Apache Tomcat: from 11.0.0-M1 through 11.0.24, from 10.1.0-M1 through 10.1.57, from 9.0.0.M1 through 9.0.120, from 8.5.0 through 8.5.100, from 7.0.0 through 7.0.109. Users are recommended to upgrade to version 11.0.25, 10.1.58, 9.0.121, which fixes the issue.
statements.impact_statement: Security constraint bypass when a `<security-constraint>` for a longer path is declared before a more restrictive constraint for a shorter sub-path in web.xml. Requires an active Tomcat servlet container evaluating security constraints against deployed web.xml descriptors. Liquibase is a CLI tool that uses picocli for command-line parsing and never starts a Spring application context or Tomcat server (grep across core/, pro/, and all extension modules for `org.apache.catalina.startup.Tomcat`, `new Tomcat(`, `TomcatServletWebServerFactory`, and `@SpringBootApplication` returns zero hits in production source). tomcat-embed-core is a transitive dependency from spring-boot-starter-web, pulled in by the Spring Boot integration module for users who embed Liquibase in their own Spring apps. No servlet container is started, so no security-constraint evaluation ever occurs.

statements.status_notes: Authentication Bypass by Capture-replay vulnerability in Apache Tomcat's DIGEST authenticator. If, before windowSize requests have been made, a client makes a DIGEST authenticated request with a nonceCount on the upper boundary of the replay window then that request is replayable once only while the associated nonceCount remains within the replay window. This issue affects Apache Tomcat: from 11.0.0-M1 through 11.0.24, from 10.1.0-M1 through 10.1.57, from 9.0.0.M1 through 9.0.120. Users are recommended to upgrade to version 11.0.25, 10.1.58 or 9.0.121, which fix the issue.
statements.impact_statement: Authentication bypass by capture-replay in Tomcat's DIGEST authenticator: a nonceCount on the upper boundary of the replay window can be replayed once before it ages out. Requires an active Tomcat servlet container with DIGEST authentication configured and processing inbound authenticated requests. Liquibase is a CLI tool that never starts a Spring application context or Tomcat server (grep across core/, pro/, and all extension modules for `org.apache.catalina.startup.Tomcat`, `new Tomcat(`, `TomcatServletWebServerFactory`, and `@SpringBootApplication` returns zero hits in production source). tomcat-embed-core is a transitive dependency from spring-boot-starter-web, pulled in by the Spring Boot integration module for users who embed Liquibase in their own Spring apps. No DIGEST authenticator is ever configured or invoked.

statements.status_notes: Expat through 2.8.3 contains a denial of service vulnerability caused by quadratic algorithmic complexity in the storeAtts() function in xmlparse.c, where processing N specified attributes with non-normalized values triggers an O(N^2) linear scan of elementType->defaultAtts to determine CDATA status. A remote unauthenticated attacker can supply a single well-formed XML document of a few megabytes to an application parsing untrusted XML to cause excessive CPU consumption, resulting in denial of service.
statements.impact_statement: This denial-of-service flaw requires an application to call libexpat's XML_Parse API on attacker-controlled XML with many non-normalized attributes. Liquibase Secure parses changelogs using the JVM's own bundled XML parser and never links against or calls system libexpat; the library ships only as an inherited base-image package and is never invoked at container runtime.

statements.status_notes: When expanding paths that begin with a tilde followed by a username, glibc's parse_tilde allocates the extracted username on the stack with strndupa based on untrusted input length. If an application passes attacker-controlled input to wordexp, an excessively long username can exhaust stack space and trigger a stack clash.
statements.impact_statement: The scanned image reports libc-bin 2.35-0ubuntu3.10, below Ubuntu's fixed 2.35-0ubuntu3.15, but this flaw requires an application to pass attacker-controlled input into glibc's wordexp path-expansion API. The stock Liquibase Secure runtime is the Liquibase Java CLI behind a bash-based entrypoint, and a source review found no references to wordexp or WRDE_APPEND in the container build or runtime path.

statements.status_notes: jackson-databind binds a JSON string to a javax.xml.datatype.Duration or javax.xml.datatype.XMLGregorianCalendar field by passing the raw string verbatim to DatatypeFactory.newDuration(value) or newXMLGregorianCalendar(value) in CoreXMLDeserializers.Std._deserialize. These deserializers are registered by default with no opt-in, so a plain ObjectMapper or JsonMapper with no polymorphic typing and no special configuration reaches this path. The XML Schema lexical grammar permits numeric components of arbitrary length, which the JDK materializes through the native BigInteger(String) and BigDecimal(String) constructors, both quadratic in digit count. Because the digits sit inside a JSON string token rather than a JSON number token, jackson-core's StreamReadConstraints.maxNumberLength guard never applies; jackson's own NumberDeserializers call validateIntegerLength or validateFPLength before parsing a stringified number, but the XML datatype deserializer omits that pre-check. An unauthenticated attacker can therefore submit a single request of a few megabytes, such as a Duration value consisting of the letter P followed by several million digits and the letter Y, and force tens of seconds to several minutes of single-threaded CPU work; a handful of concurrent requests can saturate a server's worker threads. This affects com.fasterxml.jackson.core:jackson-databind from 2.0.0 before 2.18.10, from 2.19.0 before 2.21.6, and from 2.22.0 before 2.22.2, and tools.jackson.core:jackson-databind from 3.0.0 before 3.1.6 and from 3.2.0 before 3.2.2. Users should upgrade to 2.18.10, 2.21.6, 2.22.2, 3.1.6, or 3.2.2.
statements.impact_statement: The vulnerable jackson-databind path requires deserializing JSON strings into javax.xml.datatype.Duration or XMLGregorianCalendar values through Jackson's default XML datatype deserializers. A source review found no production code that references either XML datatype anywhere in this repository. The Jackson call sites deserialize into JSON trees, generic Object or Map structures, or application-specific types that do not use those XML datatypes, so the vulnerable BigInteger and BigDecimal parsing path is not exercised by Liquibase Secure's own code. That first-party review does not by itself cover the whole product, because the distribution carries jackson-databind in more than one place. Every copy in the built distribution was read from its PackageVersion class rather than from the dependency graph, since a copy relocated inside a vendor uber-jar does not appear in a POM or a dependency tree. The first-party copies - liquibase-commercial, liquibase-commercial-mongodb, liquibase-azure, liquibase-aws-extension, liquibase-commercial-bigquery and liquibase-commercial-cassandra - are all on the fixed 2.22.2, and liquibase-commercial-cassandra's Jackson 3 copy is on the fixed 3.2.2. Three copies are relocated inside vendor drivers. snowflake-jdbc bundles 2.18.10, which is a fixed release. liquibase-commercial-couchbase bundled an affected 2.21.5 via core-io 3.12.2 and now bundles the fixed 2.21.6, because couchbase-client.version was raised to 3.12.3 at pom.xml:116. liquibase-commercial-databricks bundles 2.18.8 under com.databricks.internal.fasterxml, which is inside the affected range and is the one copy that remains. It cannot be fixed by a version pin: the latest published databricks-jdbc, 3.4.3, still bundles 2.18.9, one patch below the 2.18.10 fix, so the upgrade has to come from the vendor. That copy is judged not reachable on its own terms rather than on the first-party review: it is private to the Databricks JDBC driver, no Liquibase code obtains an ObjectMapper from it or binds JSON through it, and the driver is reached only for Databricks connections, over which Liquibase sends SQL and reads result sets rather than deserializing attacker-supplied JSON into XML datatype fields.

statements.status_notes: jackson-databind binds a JSON string to a javax.xml.datatype.Duration or javax.xml.datatype.XMLGregorianCalendar field by passing the raw string verbatim to DatatypeFactory.newDuration(value) or newXMLGregorianCalendar(value). These deserializers are registered by default with no opt-in. The XML Schema lexical grammar permits numeric components of arbitrary length, which the JDK materializes through the native BigInteger(String) and BigDecimal(String) constructors, both quadratic in digit count, and because the digits sit inside a JSON string token rather than a JSON number token the maxNumberLength guard never applies. This affects tools.jackson.core:jackson-databind from 3.0.0 before 3.1.6 and from 3.2.0 before 3.2.2. Users should upgrade to 3.1.6 or 3.2.2.
statements.impact_statement: The same advisory covers the Jackson 3 coordinate, which is a separate artifact from com.fasterxml.jackson.core:jackson-databind and carries its own version line, so it is assessed here rather than folded into the Jackson 2 entry. Liquibase Secure ships one Jackson 3 copy, in liquibase-commercial-cassandra, and it is on the fixed 3.2.2. That was read out of the built distribution rather than from the dependency graph: internal/extensions/liquibase-commercial-cassandra.jar carries META-INF/maven/tools.jackson.core/jackson-databind/pom.properties with version=3.2.2, and the constant in tools/jackson/databind/cfg/PackageVersion agrees. jackson-core in the same jar is also 3.2.2. The reachability argument is the same as for Jackson 2 and holds independently of the version: no production code in this repository references javax.xml.datatype.Duration or XMLGregorianCalendar, so the XML datatype deserializers that carry the unbounded parse are never given a target to bind. One thing to watch rather than a present exposure: no POM here pins tools.jackson.core. The version arrives transitively from com.ing.data:cassandra-jdbc-wrapper, pinned at 5.0.3 via cassandra-jdbc.version, and only that release carries a fixed Jackson. Wrapper 5.0.2 and 5.0.1 declare 3.2.0 and wrapper 5.0.0 declares 3.1.3, both inside the affected ranges, so a wrapper change could reintroduce an affected copy with no POM edit here to signal it.

statements.status_notes: Incorrect Authorization vulnerability in Apache Tomcat's FORM authentication process allows the bypassing of a security constraint that limits user access to a resource via POST but not GET. This issue affects Apache Tomcat: from 11.0.0-M1 through 11.0.24, from 10.1.0-M1 through 10.1.57, from 9.0.0.M1 through 9.0.120. Users are recommended to upgrade to version 11.0.25, 10.1.58 or 9.0.121, which fixes the issue.
statements.impact_statement: Incorrect Authorization in Tomcat's FORM authentication process allows bypassing a security constraint that limits a user to POST access on a resource (not GET). Requires an active Tomcat servlet container with FORM authentication and a POST-only security constraint configured. Liquibase is a CLI tool that never starts a Spring application context or Tomcat server (grep across core/, pro/, and all extension modules for `org.apache.catalina.startup.Tomcat`, `new Tomcat(`, `TomcatServletWebServerFactory`, and `@SpringBootApplication` returns zero hits in production source). tomcat-embed-core is a transitive dependency from spring-boot-starter-web, pulled in by the Spring Boot integration module for users who embed Liquibase in their own Spring apps. No FORM authenticator or security constraint is ever configured.

statements.status_notes: Rejected reason: ** REJECT ** DO NOT USE THIS CANDIDATE NUMBER. ConsultIDs: CVE-2026-14803. Reason: This candidate is a duplicate of CVE-2026-14803. Notes: All CVE users should reference CVE-2026-14803 instead of this candidate.
statements.impact_statement: NVD/Ubuntu list this id as REJECTED -- a duplicate of CVE-2026-14803, which describes an issue in libmojolicious-perl, not perl-base (likely a scanner package mismatch). Regardless, nothing in this repository or docker-entrypoint.sh shells out to perl.

statements.status_notes: HTTP::Tiny versions before 0.095 for Perl forward credential headers to cross-origin redirect targets. When the server returns a 3xx redirect, the caller's Authorization, Cookie and Proxy-Authorization headers are re-sent to whatever host the redirect names, across scheme, host or port boundaries, including https to http downgrades that expose them in plaintext on the wire.
statements.impact_statement: Scanner package misattribution. The vulnerable code is the HTTP::Tiny module, which Ubuntu ships in perl-modules (and libhttp-tiny-perl), not in perl-base. Neither package is installed in any Liquibase Secure image: perl-base carries only the interpreter and a minimal core module set, there is no HTTP/Tiny.pm anywhere on the image, and loading HTTP::Tiny fails with "Can't locate HTTP/Tiny.pm". The scanner matched a fix in the perl source package to perl-base, which does not contain the vulnerable module. Even setting that aside, nothing in the runtime path executes perl. Ubuntu fixes this in perl 5.38.2-3.2ubuntu0.4 (noble); jammy has no fix yet.

statements.status_notes: Vulnerability in the Oracle Java SE, Oracle GraalVM for JDK, Oracle GraalVM Enterprise Edition product of Oracle Java SE (component: JSSE). Supported versions that are affected are Oracle Java SE: 8u501, 11.0.32, 17.0.20, 21.0.12, 25.0.4, 26.0.2; Oracle GraalVM for JDK: 17.0.20 and 21.0.12; Oracle GraalVM Enterprise Edition: 21.3.19. Easily exploitable vulnerability allows unauthenticated attacker with network access via TLS to compromise Oracle Java SE, Oracle GraalVM for JDK, Oracle GraalVM Enterprise Edition. Successful attacks of this vulnerability can result in unauthorized ability to cause a partial denial of service (partial DOS) of Oracle Java SE, Oracle GraalVM for JDK, Oracle GraalVM Enterprise Edition. Note: This vulnerability can only be exploited by supplying data to APIs in the specified Component without using Untrusted Java Web Start applications or Untrusted Java applets, such as through a web service. CVSS 3.1 Base Score 5.3 (Availability impacts). CVSS Vector: (CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:N/A:L).
statements.impact_statement: JDK TLS server (JSSE) component vulnerability, part of Oracle's August 2026 CPU. Liquibase Secure is built from eclipse-temurin:21-jre-noble (docker/Dockerfile:2) and never listens on a socket; it is only an outbound network client (HTTPS to license/hub endpoints, TLS JDBC to target databases). Triggering this requires a compromised or MITM'd peer that Liquibase already trusts and connects to -- not exploitable by an arbitrary remote attacker with no foothold on those endpoints. Fixed upstream in Temurin 21.0.12.1+1, but no eclipse-temurin Docker Hub image publishes that build yet as of 2026-09-22 (all noble/jre/jdk tags remain 21.0.12_8); revisit once Temurin ships an updated 21-jre-noble tag.

statements.status_notes: sqlparse: Quadratic O(n²) denial of service in group_comments. This issue is fixed in version 0.6.0.
statements.impact_statement: sqlparse is pinned at 0.5.3 in tools/liquibase-checks/liquibase-checks/pom.xml:864. The surrounding build plugin comment states these Python packages are only needed at build time and are never used at runtime (tools/liquibase-checks/liquibase-checks/pom.xml:893, tools/liquibase-checks/liquibase-checks/pom.xml:895), and the runtime implementation only references sqlparse in explanatory comments about a possible Python lock hang (tools/liquibase-checks/liquibase-checks/src/main/java/com/liquibase/executor/PythonScriptExecutor.java:77, tools/liquibase-checks/liquibase-checks/src/main/java/com/liquibase/executor/PythonScriptExecutor.java:240). The only actual import is in a test fixture (tools/liquibase-checks/liquibase-checks/src/test/resources/scripts/badScript.py:4). NVD and GitHub both describe this as a sqlparse DoS fixed in 0.6.0, but the vulnerable parser is not reachable from the Liquibase runtime.

statements.status_notes: Successfully using libcurl to do a transfer over one HTTP proxy with Digest authentication and then changing the proxy host for a second transfer while reusing the same handle can cause libcurl to pass the Proxy-Authorization header intended for the first proxy to the second.
statements.impact_statement: The scanned image reports curl 7.81.0-1ubuntu1.20, below Ubuntu's fixed 7.81.0-1ubuntu1.24, but this issue requires a libcurl-based application to reuse the same handle across multiple proxy hosts with Digest authentication enabled. Liquibase Secure's stock container uses wget for downloads and executes the Liquibase Java CLI at runtime, and a focused review found no proxy-authenticated libcurl flow, Digest-proxy handling, or curl handle reuse path in the container build or runtime entrypoint.

statements.status_notes: libexpat before 2.8.3 has an out-of-bounds read and resultant infinite loop because low surrogates are treated the same as high surrogates during Unicode processing in the *_toUtf16 functions.
statements.impact_statement: This out-of-bounds read requires an application to call libexpat's internal *_toUtf16 Unicode conversion functions on attacker-controlled surrogate pairs. Liquibase Secure parses changelogs using the JVM's own bundled XML parser and never links against or calls system libexpat.

statements.status_notes: Netty is an asynchronous, event-driven network application framework. Prior to versions 4.1.136.Final and 4.2.16.Final, io.netty.handler.codec.dns.AbstractDnsRecord, io.netty.handler.codec.dns.DefaultDnsRecordDecoder.decodeRecord(), and io.netty.handler.codec.dns.DnsCodecUtil.decompressDomainName() failed to release retained or newly allocated ByteBuf objects when IDN.toASCII() or encodeDomainName() rejected a malformed domain name, allowing unauthenticated remote DNS packets to leak direct memory incrementally until denial of service. Fixed in 4.1.136.Final and 4.2.16.Final.
statements.impact_statement: netty-resolver-dns:4.1.135.Final (below the 4.1.136.Final fix line) resolves for this module via reactor-netty-http:1.2.18 -> reactor-netty-core:1.2.18, and unlike the other Netty CVEs assessed here, is genuinely wired into every outbound connection by default via reactor-netty-core's NameResolverProvider — this is not a code-not-reachable case. The hostname resolved is always operator-supplied configuration, never derived from changelog content: Key Vault modifiers parse the vault host from a Liquibase configuration value, and Blob Storage access uses a separately configured storage-account property, so an attacker can't inject a resolution target purely via a malicious changelog. That only rules out attacker-chosen domains, though — it doesn't rule out this CVE's actual mechanism, a malformed DNS response to an otherwise-legitimate query. DNS isn't TLS-authenticated the way this module's HTTP/2 traffic is, so the "trusted endpoint" argument used for the HTTP/2 CVEs on this module doesn't transfer here. Exploitation requires network-level access to the deployment's DNS resolution path — an assumption about the deployment environment this codebase can't verify. No newer reactor-netty release exists yet with a fixed Netty.

statements.status_notes: A signed integer overflow when sizing the destination buffer for Unicode output in ASN1_mbstring_ncopy can lead to a heap buffer overflow. The issue requires an application to call ASN1_mbstring_copy or ASN1_mbstring_ncopy directly, or to register a custom string type via ASN1_STRING_TABLE_add with attacker-controlled input large enough to overflow the size calculation.
statements.impact_statement: The scanned image reports libssl3 3.0.2-0ubuntu1.19, below Ubuntu's fixed 3.0.2-0ubuntu1.25, but this issue requires an application to call OpenSSL's ASN1_mbstring_copy or ASN1_mbstring_ncopy APIs directly, or to register a custom string type and then feed it extremely large attacker-controlled input. Liquibase Secure's stock container runs the Liquibase Java CLI rather than OpenSSL string-processing APIs, and a source review found no references to those OpenSSL ASN.1 entry points in the product runtime path.

statements.status_notes: Netty is an asynchronous, event-driven network application framework. Prior to 4.1.137.Final and 4.2.17.Final, io.netty.handler.ssl.SslClientHelloHandler#decode checks the wrong offset before reading the four-byte TLS handshake header, so a ClientHello whose handshake header spans records can cause an IndexOutOfBoundsException and invoke select(ctx, null). This selects the default SslContext instead of the SNI-specific context. In deployments where per-SNI clientAuth=REQUIRE is the sole mutual TLS gate, the default SslContext uses clientAuth=NONE or clientAuth=OPTIONAL, and no application-layer certificate verification exists, an unauthenticated remote attacker can bypass the protected route's mutual TLS requirement. This issue is fixed in versions 4.1.137.Final and 4.2.17.Final.
statements.impact_statement: SslClientHelloHandler#decode checks the wrong offset before reading the four-byte TLS handshake header, so a ClientHello whose handshake header spans records can throw IndexOutOfBoundsException and fall back to the default SslContext instead of the SNI-specific one. This only becomes an mTLS bypass in a deployment that (a) runs a Netty server accepting inbound TLS connections, (b) uses per-SNI SslContext selection as the sole mutual-TLS gate (clientAuth=REQUIRE on the SNI context, weaker on the default), and (c) has no application-layer certificate check. Liquibase never runs a Netty server: a grep across all Java sources for ServerBootstrap, NioServerSocketChannel, SniHandler, AbstractSniHandler, and SslClientHelloHandler returns zero hits: netty-handler is present only as a transitive dependency of outbound HTTP/TLS clients (Azure SDK's azure-core-http-netty, the AWS SDK, the Couchbase client, the Cassandra JDBC driver). The scanner found netty-handler below the fixed versions in five bundled jars (Docker Scan run https://github.com/liquibase/liquibase-pro/actions/runs/34365994421): liquibase-commercial-cassandra.jar 4.1.119.Final, liquibase-azure.jar 4.1.135.Final, liquibase-aws-extension.jar 4.1.136.Final, liquibase-commercial-couchbase.jar 4.2.16.Final, and liquibase-azure-deps.jar (unlabeled in the scan, same shaded copy as liquibase-azure.jar); none of them run a Netty server, so the version gap does not matter to this assessment.

statements.status_notes: Netty is an asynchronous, event-driven network application framework. Prior to 4.1.137.Final and 4.2.17.Final, the default SniHandler constructors use pre-handshake ClientHello aggregation implemented in SslClientHelloHandler, which repeatedly recopies all previously received bytes each time it processes another fragment of a ClientHello split across TLS records. An unauthenticated attacker can advertise a large ClientHello and deliver it in thousands of tiny records, causing quadratic CPU consumption on the event loop and degrading TLS handling for other clients. Fixed in versions 4.1.137.Final and 4.2.17.Final.
statements.impact_statement: This CVE affects the same pre-handshake ClientHello aggregation code in SslClientHelloHandler as CVE-2026-75595, already assessed in this file: a server-side SNI-routing feature that repeatedly recopies buffered bytes while reassembling a fragmented ClientHello, causing quadratic CPU consumption when an attacker splits a large ClientHello across many small TLS records. This only matters to a deployment running a Netty server with per-SNI SslContext selection (SniHandler/AbstractSniHandler). A source review found no references to ServerBootstrap, NioServerSocketChannel, SniHandler, AbstractSniHandler, or SslClientHelloHandler anywhere in this repository; netty-handler is present only as a transitive dependency of outbound HTTP/TLS clients (the AWS SDK's netty-nio-client, the Azure SDK's azure-core-http-netty, the Couchbase Java client, and the Cassandra driver's own AWS SDK chain), none of which run a Netty server. The AWS extension already resolves netty-handler at 4.1.137.Final, past the fix line, as defense-in-depth; the Azure extension remains on 4.1.135.Final, the Cassandra extension on 4.1.130.Final, and the Couchbase client's shaded copy on 4.2.16.Final, all relying solely on the reachability argument.

statements.status_notes: For ChaCha20-Poly1305 and AES-OCB, EVP_Cipher could report successful decryption for an empty ciphertext without verifying the supplied AEAD tag. Applications that rely on EVP_Cipher to validate the tag in that case might accept forged messages.
statements.impact_statement: The scanned image reports libssl3 3.0.2-0ubuntu1.19, below Ubuntu's fixed 3.0.2-0ubuntu1.29, but this issue requires an application to use OpenSSL's EVP_Cipher one-shot API for ChaCha20-Poly1305 or AES-OCB decryption on an empty ciphertext while expecting that call to validate the AEAD tag. Liquibase Secure's stock container runs the Liquibase Java CLI rather than OpenSSL AEAD decryption helpers, and a source review found no references to EVP_Cipher, ChaCha20-Poly1305, or AES-OCB in the product runtime path.

statements.status_notes: A CMP client that identifies the certificate to revoke with a PKCS#10 CSR dereferences a NULL pointer and crashes when a malicious or compromised CMP server returns a crafted name in the revocation response. The response passes message-protection checks before the affected code runs, so the attacker must control the server or hold the protection secret.
statements.impact_statement: No process in the Liquibase Secure runtime path links OpenSSL: the JRE uses its own Java TLS and crypto providers and none of its native libraries link libssl or libcrypto, lpm is a statically linked Go binary, and the only binaries in the image that do link libssl or libcrypto (the wget, curl and openssl command-line tools, plus the coreutils digest utilities on noble) are never invoked after the image is built. Liquibase Secure contains no CMP client, so OpenSSL's revocation response handling is never reached. Fixed in Ubuntu libssl3 3.0.2-0ubuntu1.30 (jammy, shipped by Liquibase Secure 5.0.0 and 5.0.1) and libssl3t64 3.0.13-0ubuntu3.16 (noble, Liquibase Secure 5.0.2 through 5.2.2); every published 5.x tag ships an older build.

statements.status_notes: Expat through 2.8.3 contains an out-of-bounds read vulnerability that allows attackers to trigger memory corruption by processing XML with external entity parsers created via XML_ExternalEntityParserCreate. A struct size mismatch between ELEMENT_TYPE members causes storeAtts to read the attIndex member past allocated memory boundaries, resulting in failure to normalize whitespace in non-CDATA attributes or a wild pointer dereference causing a segfault. This vulnerability was introduced by the fix for CVE-2026-66046.
statements.impact_statement: This out-of-bounds read requires an application to call libexpat's XML_ExternalEntityParserCreate API to parse attacker-controlled XML. Liquibase Secure parses changelogs using the JVM's own bundled XML parser and never links against or calls system libexpat; the library ships only as an inherited base-image package and is never invoked at container runtime.

statements.status_notes: util-linux versions through 2.41.5 and 2.42.2 fail to check mount helper exit status before running post-mount hooks, allowing unprivileged users to execute privileged operations on pre-existing filesystems. Attackers can exploit X-mount.idmap or X-mount.owner hooks to clone filesystems with inherited suid bits or modify target inode permissions after a helper fails, achieving privilege escalation.
statements.impact_statement: util-linux fails to check mount helper exit status before running post- mount hooks, allowing unprivileged users to execute privileged operations on pre-existing files (local privilege escalation on a multi- user host). Nothing in this image's runtime calls mount or nsenter; the container runs a single fixed non-root user with no multi-user or fstab- controlled surface.

statements.status_notes: libexpat before 2.8.4 lacks handler call depth tracking with custom encoding callbacks. Thus, a use-after-free can occur.
statements.impact_statement: This use-after-free requires an application to register a custom encoding callback with libexpat, a pattern specific to applications embedding libexpat directly. Liquibase Secure parses changelogs using the JVM's own bundled XML parser and never links against or calls system libexpat.

statements.status_notes: Converting crafted SHIFT_JISX0213 input to UCS-4 or the internal wide character encoding, for example with iconv, in the GNU C Library version 2.3 to 2.44 may result in the converter making no progress, causing the calling application to hang.
statements.impact_statement: The scanned image reports libc-bin 2.35-0ubuntu3.10, below Ubuntu's fixed 2.35-0ubuntu3.15, but this issue requires an application to feed attacker-controlled SHIFT_JISX0213 data through glibc's iconv conversion path with a small enough output buffer to split a two-code-point decode. Liquibase Secure's stock runtime path is the Java CLI, and a review of its build and runtime flow found no references to iconv or SHIFT_JISX0213 processing. The vulnerable glibc conversion path is not reachable from Liquibase Secure.

statements.status_notes: jackson-databind contains the general-purpose data-binding functionality and tree-model for Jackson Data Processor. Prior to versions 2.18.9, 2.21.5, 2.22.1, 3.1.5, and 3.2.1 on their respective release lines, the java.net.InetAddress branch of FromStringDeserializer.Std._deserialize() calls InetAddress.getByName() on attacker-controlled input, causing eager DNS resolution during deserialization and enabling DNS-based server-side request forgery and internal-host enumeration. This issue is fixed in versions 2.18.9, 2.21.5, 2.22.1, 3.1.5, and 3.2.1.
statements.impact_statement: Fixed in jackson-databind 2.18.9, 2.21.5 and 2.22.1. Every published Liquibase Secure image from 5.0.0 through 6.0.0 carries at least one copy inside the advisory range, so this assessment does not rest on version. The copies were read from the PackageVersion class in each shipped jar, including copies relocated inside vendor drivers. From 5.0.0 through 5.2.1 every copy is affected, first-party and vendor alike. In 5.2.2 and 6.0.0 the first-party copies are fixed and the one affected copy left is 2.18.8, relocated inside databricks-jdbc. The vulnerable path is reached only when Jackson binds a JSON string to a java.net.InetAddress target, at which point the standard deserializer calls InetAddress.getByName() on it. No Liquibase code binds JSON to an InetAddress. Its only InetAddress uses are local host-name lookups and a loopback check on a configured JDBC host, none of them through Jackson, and no Liquibase type that Jackson binds has an InetAddress field. The relocated vendor copies are private to their drivers. Liquibase never hands them JSON, and the drivers use them for their own protocol messages with the database service.

statements.status_notes: SM2 signature generation in OpenSSL uses variable-time BIGNUM operations on the secret nonce and the private key, so signing time depends on secret values. An attacker able to measure SM2 signing times can learn information about the per-signature nonce and, over many signatures, recover the private key.

Liquibase Secure never performs SM2 signing through OpenSSL. statements.status_notes: The nsenter --join-cgroup option opens the target cgroup.procs file as root and leaves that file descriptor open across later namespace and credential changes and across execve(). Because the kernel checks later cgroup migrations using the credentials from the original open, a program run in an attacker-controlled target can inherit root's ability to move host processes between cgroups. After a privileged operator uses --join-cgroup against that target, an unprivileged user can migrate and terminate unrelated root processes.
statements.impact_statement: nsenter --join-cgroup opens the target cgroup.procs file as root and leaves the descriptor open across later namespace/credential changes and execve() (local privilege escalation). Nothing in this image's runtime calls nsenter; the container runs a single fixed non-root user with no multi-user surface.

statements.status_notes: The X-mount.subdir option uses a detached-tree fast path on Linux 6.15 and later and passes the configured subdirectory to open_tree() with AT_SYMLINK_NOFOLLOW. That flag does not stop intermediate symlink traversal or keep resolution inside the newly mounted filesystem. A local unprivileged user with an fstab-authorized X-mount.subdir entry can attach a host path at the intended mountpoint.

statements.impact_statement: The X-mount.subdir option uses a detached-tree fast path with AT_SYMLINK_NOFOLLOW that does not stop intermediate symlink traversal (local privilege escalation; Ubuntu rates Medium, upstream CVSS is High at 7.0). Nothing in this image's runtime calls mount; the container runs a single fixed non-root user with no multi-user surface.

statements.status_notes: A flaw was found in util-linux. Restricted bind mounts take the source path from fstab but do not pin that source before the privileged mount. A local unprivileged user who can replace the authorized source or a writable ancestor can redirect SUID mount(8) to bind another host directory. If the fstab entry also sets X-mount.owner, X-mount.group, or X-mount.mode, root then changes ownership or mode on that redirected inode.
statements.impact_statement: Restricted bind mounts take the source path from fstab without pinning it before the privileged mount, allowing a local unprivileged user to redirect the mount target (local privilege escalation). Nothing in this image's runtime reads fstab or calls mount; the container runs a single fixed non-root user.

statements.status_notes: When CURLOPT_PINNEDPUBLICKEY is configured alongside options that disable standard peer verification (CURLOPT_SSL_VERIFYPEER = 0 and CURLOPT_SSL_VERIFYHOST = 0), libcurl fails to enforce public key pinning on connections established without a presented server certificate, allowing unauthenticated connections to succeed when they should be rejected.
statements.impact_statement: This flaw requires an application to configure libcurl with CURLOPT_PINNEDPUBLICKEY alongside disabled peer verification options. Liquibase Secure's runtime process tree never links against libcurl; curl ships only as an inherited base-image package and is never invoked at container runtime.

statements.status_notes: Converting crafted EUC_JISX0213 input to UCS-4 or the internal wide character encoding, for example with iconv, in the GNU C Library version 2.3 to 2.44 may result in the converter making no progress, causing the calling application to hang.
statements.impact_statement: The scanned image reports libc-bin 2.35-0ubuntu3.10, below Ubuntu's fixed 2.35-0ubuntu3.15, but this issue requires an application to feed attacker-controlled EUC_JISX0213 data through glibc's iconv conversion path with a small enough output buffer to split a two-code-point decode. Liquibase Secure's stock runtime path is the Java CLI, and a review of its build and runtime flow found no references to iconv or EUC_JISX0213 processing. The vulnerable glibc conversion path is not reachable from Liquibase Secure.

statements.status_notes: When libpsl support is enabled, libcurl fails to enforce the Public Suffix List boundary check when processing a Set-Cookie header where the Domain attribute explicitly matches an origin host that is itself a public suffix. Instead of coercing it into a strict host-only cookie, libcurl saves the cookie with wildcard domain scope, inappropriately including it in subsequent outbound requests or HTTP redirects to arbitrary sibling subdomains under the same public suffix.
statements.impact_statement: This flaw requires an application to build libcurl with libpsl support and process attacker-controlled Set-Cookie responses. Liquibase Secure's runtime process tree never links against libcurl; curl ships only as an inherited base-image package and is never invoked at container runtime.

statements.status_notes: Pod::Text versions before 6.1.1 for Perl allow CPU and memory exhaustion formatting a POD document whose =over nesting drives the margin to the output width. Each =over adds its indent to the margin, which wrap() subtracts from the output width to get the space available for text. When that space reaches zero, the line-splitting substitution matches the empty string, and the loop consumes no input while appending the margin padding on every pass. Formatting an attacker-supplied POD document never returns, and the output grows until memory is exhausted.
statements.impact_statement: Pod::Text (bundled with perl-base) CPU/memory exhaustion formatting a crafted POD document. Nothing in this repository or docker-entrypoint.sh shells out to perl or invokes POD formatting (pod2text/perldoc); the entrypoint does its own pattern matching with bash case/glob syntax.

statements.status_notes: A new transfer that uses STARTTLS to upgrade the connection might reuse an existing live connection even though the TLS configuration mismatches and the connection should not have been reused.
statements.impact_statement: The scanned image reports curl 7.81.0-1ubuntu1.20, below Ubuntu's fixed 7.81.0-1ubuntu1.25, but this issue requires a libcurl-based application to upgrade a connection with STARTTLS and then incorrectly reuse a live connection whose TLS settings no longer match. Liquibase Secure's stock container uses wget for its own downloads and executes the Liquibase Java CLI at runtime, and a focused review found no STARTTLS, curl connection-pool, or libcurl TLS-reuse path in the container build or runtime entrypoint.

statements.status_notes: DefaultBaseTypeLimitingValidator is the PolymorphicTypeValidator applied automatically whenever @JsonTypeInfo is used without an explicitly configured custom validator. It denies polymorphic resolution only for a fixed set of "unsafe base types", and its isSafeSubType method returns true unconditionally for every base type outside that set. java.lang.Comparable was absent from the list despite being implemented by a very large fraction of JDK and application classes, comparable in breadth to java.io.Serializable, which is on the list for that reason. An application declaring an @JsonTypeInfo-annotated property or class with Comparable as its base type, and no custom PolymorphicTypeValidator, will accept a type identifier for essentially any class implementing Comparable. This yields an attacker-controlled object instantiation primitive; a demonstrated case constructs a java.io.File for an arbitrary attacker-chosen path, which becomes path-traversal-adjacent if the application subsequently calls path-sensitive methods on the value. No class implementing Comparable has been identified that yields code execution through deserialization alone. Global Default Typing via activateDefaultTyping is not affected, because that method structurally requires an explicit PolymorphicTypeValidator argument. This affects com.fasterxml.jackson.core:jackson-databind from 2.11.0 before 2.18.10, from 2.19.0 before 2.21.6, and from 2.22.0 before 2.22.2, and tools.jackson.core:jackson-databind from 3.0.0 before 3.1.6 and from 3.2.0 before 3.2.2. Users should upgrade to 2.18.10, 2.21.6, 2.22.2, 3.1.6, or 3.2.2.
statements.impact_statement: The vulnerable DefaultBaseTypeLimitingValidator path is exercised only when an application declares @JsonTypeInfo on a property or class whose base type is java.lang.Comparable and lets Jackson fall back to the default validator. An inspection of every jar in the shipped distribution, including the Jackson copies relocated inside the couchbase, databricks and snowflake drivers and the license-tracking application, found @JsonTypeInfo declared on exactly three base types, Apache Arrow's ArrowType (bundled by bigquery, databricks and snowflake) and Couchbase's AnalyticsLink and BucketConfig, plus a reflective lookup of the annotation in Azure Core's FlatteningDeserializer. None of these base types is Comparable, and all of them bind JSON that comes from the respective database or cloud service, not from Liquibase users. Liquibase Secure's own code never uses @JsonTypeInfo. Fixed in jackson-databind 2.18.10, 2.21.6 and 2.22.2. Every Liquibase Secure release from 5.0.0 through 5.2.2 ships in-range copies, read from the PackageVersion class of each copy in the built distribution rather than from the dependency graph: 5.2.2 carries 2.22.1 in the aws, azure, bigquery, cassandra and mongodb extensions and in liquibase-azure-deps, 2.21.5 relocated inside the couchbase driver, 2.18.9 relocated inside snowflake-jdbc and 2.18.8 relocated inside databricks-jdbc. The next release moves the pinned copies to 2.22.2; the relocated driver copies follow their vendors' releases.

statements.status_notes: Perl versions before 5.40.5-RC1, from 5.41.0 before 5.42.3-RC1, from 5.43.0 before 5.43.11 have a heap buffer overflow when compiling regular expressions with a repeated fixed string on 32-bit builds. A caller that compiles an attacker-controlled regular expression on a 32-bit perl build triggers a heap buffer overflow at compile time.
statements.impact_statement: The heap overflow only exists on 32-bit Perl builds compiling an attacker-controlled regular expression. Liquibase Secure images are published only for linux/amd64 and linux/arm64, and the shipped perl is a 64-bit build (pointer size 8). In addition, nothing in the runtime path executes perl: the container entrypoint and the liquibase launcher script contain no perl invocation, the Liquibase CLI is a Java process, and lpm is a statically linked Go binary. Fixed in Ubuntu perl-base 5.34.0-3ubuntu1.7 (jammy, Liquibase Secure 5.0.0 and 5.0.1 shipped 5.34.0-3ubuntu1.5) and 5.38.2-3.2ubuntu0.3 (noble, Liquibase Secure 5.0.2 through 5.2.1 shipped 5.38.2-3.2ubuntu0.2); Liquibase Secure 5.2.2 and later ship 5.38.2-3.2ubuntu0.6.

statements.status_notes: sqlparse is a non-validating SQL parser module for Python. Prior to 0.6.0, sqlparse.format(sql, reindent=True) and sqlformat --reindent route attacker-controlled parenthesized tuple lists through ReindentFilter._get_offset() in sqlparse/filters/reindent.py, where _flatten_up_to_token() repeatedly rebuilds and joins the statement prefix. Thousands of offset calculations walk an expanding token tree, producing quadratic CPU consumption for inputs that remain below MAX_GROUPING_TOKENS and causing request delays, reduced throughput, or worker starvation. This issue is fixed in version 0.6.0.
statements.impact_statement: sqlparse ships in the runtime virtual environment of the checks module's embedded Python scripting engine, which end users can use to author custom check scripts; the build only strips pip, setuptools, and their installer machinery from that environment, not sqlparse itself. None of the check scripts Liquibase bundles and runs by default import sqlparse — they use a different SQL parsing library for changeset SQL. The vulnerable reindent code path (sqlparse.format(sql, reindent=True) or sqlformat --reindent) is only reachable if a customer authors and configures their own custom check script that imports sqlparse and calls it in that mode against attacker-influenced SQL; no shipped configuration does this out of the box.

statements.status_notes: libcurl might reuse the wrong connection when asked to perform Negotiate-authenticated requests, even when those requests are set to use different services.
statements.impact_statement: The scanned image reports curl 7.81.0-1ubuntu1.20, below Ubuntu's fixed 7.81.0-1ubuntu1.25, but this issue requires a libcurl-based application to reuse pooled connections across Negotiate-authenticated requests that change the target service. Liquibase Secure's stock container uses wget for downloads and executes the Liquibase Java CLI at runtime, and a focused review found no Negotiate-authenticated libcurl flow, service- aware connection reuse, or curl handle pool in the container build or runtime entrypoint.

statements.status_notes: OpenSSL's DTLS retransmission logic mishandles a handshake message write that was suspended part-way through: the retransmitted message is read from a stale buffer offset and overwrites the state the suspended write needs to resume. A peer can receive heap memory as plaintext handshake data, or the read can reach unmapped memory and crash the process.
statements.impact_statement: No process in the Liquibase Secure runtime path links OpenSSL: the JRE uses its own Java TLS and crypto providers and none of its native libraries link libssl or libcrypto, lpm is a statically linked Go binary, and the only binaries in the image that do link libssl or libcrypto (the wget, curl and openssl command-line tools, plus the coreutils digest utilities on noble) are never invoked after the image is built. OpenSSL's DTLS implementation is therefore never used by Liquibase Secure, and no DTLS handshake can be in flight for the retransmission logic to act on. Fixed in Ubuntu libssl3 3.0.2-0ubuntu1.30 (jammy, shipped by Liquibase Secure 5.0.0 and 5.0.1) and libssl3t64 3.0.13-0ubuntu3.16 (noble, Liquibase Secure 5.0.2 through 5.2.2); every published 5.x tag ships an older build.

statements.status_notes: zlib versions 1.3.1.2 through 1.3.2 contain a heap buffer overflow vulnerability in the gz_vacate() function when processing non-blocking gzwrite() operations with stale external buffer pointers. Attackers can trigger the overflow by calling gzprintf() or gzvprintf() after a write stall, causing an unchecked memmove() to write beyond the internal input buffer boundary.
statements.impact_statement: This heap buffer overflow requires an application to call system zlib's gzwrite/gzprintf APIs in a non-blocking configuration after a write stall. The JVM's own zip/gzip native code (libzip.so) bundles its own zip/deflate implementation and does not dynamically link against the system zlib package; a review of the JVM's native library dependencies confirmed no linkage against libz.

statements.status_notes: PCRE2 before 10.48 allows a pcre2_dfa_match out-of-bounds write because reuse of a cached workspace block, in a recursive DFA matching workspace, lacks a size check (even though a newly allocated block, for the same purpose, does have a size check). This outcome requires an attacker-controlled regular expression, or a recursive pattern in conjunction with a small heap limit (this can be set through the API).
statements.impact_statement: PCRE2 pcre2_dfa_match out-of-bounds write via cached workspace reuse, fixed upstream in PCRE2 10.48 but not yet backported to Ubuntu noble. Liquibase is a pure-Java application (java.util.regex) with no linkage to native libpcre2, and docker-entrypoint.sh performs no regex or grep operations.

statements.status_notes: Initializing the DNS stub resolver from an /etc/resolv.conf file, or a LOCALDOMAIN environment variable, whose search list contains a domain of roughly 200 characters or more in the GNU C Library version 2.26 to 2.44 results in an assertion failure which aborts the process. The resolver truncates the search list when copying it into the fixed-size _res.defdname buffer, then asserts that the copy is consistent with the full configuration. The consistency check compared against the wrong size and did not handle a first entry that does not fit, so a correctly truncated list failed the assertion. Any process that resolves names through the library is affected, including long-running processes that reload /etc/resolv.conf on the next query after it changes. Search domains are commonly written to /etc/resolv.conf from data received over DHCP or from a VPN server, so an attacker on the local network may be able to trigger this without privileges on the target system, subject to validation by the network configuration software.
statements.impact_statement: glibc DNS stub resolver assertion-abort issue when /etc/resolv.conf or LOCALDOMAIN contains a ~200+ character search-list domain. Requires attacker control of the container's DNS configuration; not remotely triggerable against this image.
